item.research_question: Can alloying be used to optimize the physical properties of tin sulfide/selenide solid solutions for energy applications?
item.material_system: Tin sulfide/selenide solid solutions, specifically Pnma and rocksalt Sn(S1–xSex), Sn(S1–xSex)2, and Sn2(S1–xSex)3
item.processing_route: High-throughput first-principles computational modeling and statistical thermodynamics, with supercell expansions and density functional theory (DFT) calculations
key_findings: The formation of Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) and Sn(S1–xSex)2 solid solutions is predicted to be facile
Rocksalt Sn(S1–xSex) solid solutions are predicted to be metastable, but may be accessible under certain synthesis conditions
Sn2(S1–xSex)3 solid solutions with low Se content are predicted to be accessible
The bandgap of the solid solutions can be tuned by varying the composition
The lattice thermal conductivity is predicted to decrease with increasing Se content
item.mechanism: The alloying of tin sulfide and selenide phases leads to a predictable variation of the bandgap, density of states, and optical properties with composition, allowing for the optimization of material properties for energy applications
item.limitations: The calculations do not include vibrational contributions to the free energy, and the lattice thermal conductivity is not directly calculated
item.future_work: The exploration of methods for analyzing more quantitatively the effect of alloying on the lattice dynamics, such as using energetics calculations to parameterize an empirical force field
quotes: alloying affords facile and precise control over the electronic, optical, and vibrational properties
the formation of Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) and Sn(S1–xSex)2 solid solutions should be facile

System: Tin sulfide/selenide solid solutions, specifically Pnma and rocksalt Sn(S1–xSex), Sn(S1–xSex)2, and Sn2(S1–xSex)3. Findings: The formation of Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) and Sn(S1–xSex)2 solid solutions is predicted to be facile; Rocksalt Sn(S1–xSex) solid solutions are predicted to be metastable, but may be accessible under certain synthesis conditions; Sn2(S1–xSex)3 solid solutions with low Se content are predicted to be accessible; The bandgap of the solid solutions can be tuned by varying the composition; The lattice thermal conductivity is predicted to decrease with increasing Se content. item.research_question: How do the thermodynamic, electronic, and vibrational properties of Snn(S1–xSex)m solid solutions change with composition, and what are the implications for energy applications?
item.material_system: Snn(S1–xSex)m solid solutions, including Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) and Sn(S1–xSex)2
key_findings: The bandgap of Sn(S1–xSex)2 can be tuned down to the theoretical optimum for photovoltaic applications
Increasing Se content in Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) decreases the bandgap, but does not significantly improve optical absorption
Alloying can allow the band levels to be adjusted for a better electrical match to other device components
The entropic stabilization obtained by alloying may reduce or prevent undesirable chemical reactions at interfaces
Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) solid solutions with high Se content can improve thermoelectric properties over the champion SnSe material
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the systematic composition dependence of the bandgap, band-edge positions, and dielectric properties in the solid solutions can be used to fine-tune optoelectronic properties for energy applications
item.limitations: The predicted metastability of the majority of the Sn2(S1–xSex)3 and all of the rocksalt Sn(S1–xSex) compositions implies that preparing and working with these materials in bulk would be challenging
item.future_work: Future developments toward quantitative modeling of the composition dependence of the lattice dynamics and thermal transport will make this a valuable addition to the growing capabilities of computational materials design
quotes: providing a means to fine-tune the optoelectronic properties for their proven photovoltaic and photocatalysis applications
the crystal growth direction could be better controlled, given the 2D structure
the full oxidation of Sn would reduce the need to tightly control the chalcogen chemical potential during synthesis

System: Snn(S1–xSex)m solid solutions, including Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) and Sn(S1–xSex)2. Findings: The bandgap of Sn(S1–xSex)2 can be tuned down to the theoretical optimum for photovoltaic applications; Increasing Se content in Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) decreases the bandgap, but does not significantly improve optical absorption; Alloying can allow the band levels to be adjusted for a better electrical match to other device components; The entropic stabilization obtained by alloying may reduce or prevent undesirable chemical reactions at interfaces; Pnma Sn(S1–xSex) solid solutions with high Se content can improve thermoelectric properties over the champion SnSe material. Limitations: The predicted metastability of the majority of the Sn2(S1–xSex)3 and all of the rocksalt Sn(S1–xSex) compositions implies that preparing and working with these materials in bulk would be challenging. Future work: Future developments toward quantitative modeling of the composition dependence of the lattice dynamics and thermal transport will make this a valuable addition to the growing capabilities of computational materials design.
